opening_message:
Ticket 1: Christopher Myers (employee ID E012) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E012.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Christopher Myers (E012) is a full-time Analyst requesting write access to Source Code. As a full-time employee, the maximum access is write (admin requires the role to own the system; Analyst does not own Source Code). The requested write level is within policy, so recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Christopher Myers (E012) is a contractor with basic security training, not full-time. Contractors with basic training max out at read access; admin is never allowed. Requested write is above the maximum, so recommend read.
reason: The two notes about E012 conflict on employment type. HR states Christopher Myers is full-time (max write), while Security states the Security DB shows contractor with basic security training (max read) and explicitly notes "not full-time." Given the direct contradiction and the security agent's explicit correction, I apply the more conservative assessment: contractor with basic training, whose maximum is read. The requested level (write) exceeds the maximum, so the granted level is read. Never granting more than requested, and erring toward least privilege when records conflict.
